role.altitude: The energy engineer keeps walking sites, judging opportunities, analysing causes and advising clients; collecting meter readings, typing up nameplates and logger files, normalising for weather in spreadsheets and writing reports from scratch shrink.
skills_to_grow: Editing drafted reports against the calculation workbook
role.ambitious_version: An engineer who spots waste the week it starts, not at the yearly review.

tasks.short: Review the site's energy profile, screen standard measures, identify site-specific savings strategies, estimate savings and payback, decide the package, and recommend it to the client.

steps.what: Engineer reviews the site's energy use profile and equipment list
Engineer screens standard energy savings measures against the site's equipment
Engineer identifies site-specific strategies for more energy-efficient operation
Engineer estimates savings and payback per measure
Engineer decides the package of measures to recommend
Engineer presents the recommendations to the client

tasks.design: The monitoring dashboard shows the site's energy profile beside its equipment register, instead of the engineer combining meter exports and equipment lists. A measures catalogue lists which standard measures apply to the site's equipment types by rule. A savings template applies energy prices and standard savings factors per measure. Identifying site-specific strategies, deciding the package and presenting stay with the engineer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Profiles were assembled by hand and each estimate built from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Monitoring dashboards, measures catalogues and savings templates.
tasks.still_hard: Process energy in industry with no standard measures.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a schedule change saves more than new equipment.
tasks.altitude: Less assembling; finding and persuading stay.

reach.learn: Whether more recommended measures are taken up.

evidence.claim: Sites above set energy use have an information duty every four years and a research duty from 10 million kWh.
Cost estimates are quantities times a price table, done deterministically.

assumptions: Boundary: identifying and recommending strategies; energy audits (task 20855) and detailed energy modelling (task 18148) are sibling tasks.

Input contract for s1: meter data from the monitoring task 18156 and an equipment register kept by the facility manager, for about 70% of sites. s1 keeps 60: combining meter exports and equipment lists goes for those sites, while reading the profile stays.
Identifying, deciding and presenting keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of sites with an equipment register.
research_questions: Are recommendations ready sooner after a site visit?

incremental.description: Engineer keeps the measures catalogue and savings factors current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: only 40% of sites have meters and a register in the dashboard, so the profile review (s1) keeps 77, and custom industrial measures mean savings estimates (s4) keep 75 (15.1); high: about 70% coverage and standard measures as assumed (21.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan the visit, inspect the site, record equipment and observations, install and remove sub-metering, and load logger data and field notes for energy conservation analyses.

steps.what: Engineer plans the site visit: what to inspect and where to meter
Engineer walks the jobsite and carries out field inspections of equipment
Engineer records nameplates and observations: on paper today, in the tablet inspection form with a nameplate photo after the change
Engineer installs and later removes sub-metering and loggers
Engineer downloads logger data and types field notes into the analysis spreadsheet

tasks.design: A tablet inspection form records each item with a nameplate photo and set fields, so the equipment list builds during the walk instead of from paper notes later. Loggers send data through a gateway to the analysis workbook, instead of being downloaded and copied one by one. Planning, inspecting and fitting sub-meters stay with the engineer. Sub-meters measure equipment, not people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Field notes and logger files were typed up after the visit.
tasks.enabler_now: Tablet inspection forms and connected loggers.
tasks.still_hard: Plant rooms without signal for the gateway.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing a valve left open that no meter shows.

evidence.claim: Records apps and integrations replace paper forms and spreadsheet glue.

assumptions: Boundary: collecting data; energy audits (task 20855) and modelling and verification (task 18148) are sibling tasks.
s3 keeps its full time: writing nameplates and observations is a first record, on a tablet instead of paper. s5 saves the second entry of paper notes and logger files.
Input contract for s5: about 70% of loggers connect through the gateway; s5 is priced at that share.
Planning, inspecting and installing keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of loggers with remote upload.
research_questions: Is data ready for analysis sooner after the visit?

incremental.description: Engineer maintains the inspection form and gateway settings.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the tablet form is used on only half of the visits and plant rooms lack signal, so typing notes and logger files (s5) keeps 60 (7.5); high: tablet form on all visits and about 70% of loggers on the gateway as assumed (13.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect meter data, normalise consumption for weather and production, review trends and flag anomalies, analyze causes of changes in energy consumption, and chart results.

steps.what: Engineer collects meter data for each site
Engineer normalises energy consumption for weather and production
Engineer reviews trends against the baseline and flags anomalies
Engineer analyzes causes of changes in consumption
Engineer charts the results for the client

tasks.design: Smart meter and sub-meter data flow from the metering provider into an energy monitoring dashboard, instead of the engineer collecting readings and exports per site. Code normalises consumption with degree-days and production figures. Rules flag deviations from each site's baseline, and the engineer reviews the flags instead of scanning every series. Analysing causes stays with the engineer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Readings were collected and normalised by hand in spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Metering data feeds and monitoring dashboards with baseline rules.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing the spike was a heat wave plus a broken valve.

ambition.what: Review consumption weekly instead of monthly.

reach.learn: Whether waste is spotted within a week.

evidence.claim: Recurring status reports become a dashboard; test data and anomalies suit dashboards and statistics.

assumptions: Boundary: monitoring and analysing consumption; verifying bills and meter readings (task 20858) and graphical representations (task 18159) are sibling tasks.
s5 is part of creating graphical representations of energy data, which sibling task 18159 covers; its saving is counted there.
Input contract for s1: smart meter data from the metering provider for about 80% of sites; s1 is priced at that share.
Analysing causes keeps its full time.
unknowns: Share of sites with smart meters.

incremental.description: Engineer maintains baselines, rules and data feeds.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: only half of the sites have smart meters, so collecting data (s1) keeps 56, and sites on monthly bills cannot be flagged by rules, so trend review (s3) keeps 75 (26.7); high: about 80% of sites on smart meters as assumed (37.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Gather project data, write the energy-related project report, fill its tables, prepare the documentation the authority requires, approve and send the report to the client, and approve and submit the authority form.

steps.what: Engineer gathers project data: measures, savings, costs and status
Engineer writes the narrative of the energy-related project reports

loop.input: The project data tables and the engineer's notes on findings.
loop.output: A draft narrative in the report template.
loop.check: Every number must match the calculation workbook, and each statement about a measure must match that measure's savings, costs and status in the workbook and say whether savings are estimated or measured; any mismatch stops the draft; unclear statements are marked for the engineer, who rewrites the findings.
loop.stop: The engineer writes the narrative by hand after two failed checks.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each project's findings and context differ.

steps.what: Engineer fills the report tables
Engineer prepares the documentation required by the energy authority
Engineer checks the final project report: text and tables match the workbook, findings say what the measured or estimated savings support, and the client addressee is right
Engineer sends the report to the client
Engineer checks the final authority form: measures, figures and site match the workbook and the report, and the form goes to the right authority scheme
Engineer submits the form to the energy authority

approvals.approved_version: The project report text and tables exactly as checked by the engineer in s5, sent once by e-mail to the client contact named in it; any edit needs a new check before sending.

The authority form with the measures and figures exactly as checked by the engineer in s7, submitted once through the energy authority's portal for the site named in it; any change needs a new check before submitting.

tasks.design: Project data come from the project tracker and the savings workbook, instead of being gathered from mails and files. The report template fills tables from the workbook, and a drafting step writes the narrative, with every number checked against the workbook. The authority form is prepared from the same measures list. The engineer approves and sends the client report, and separately approves and submits the authority form.
tasks.previous_blocker: Data were gathered by hand and reports written from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Report templates fed by the workbook and drafting checked against it.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining to a client why savings came in lower.
tasks.altitude: Less assembling and typing; judgement and sign-off stay.

evidence.claim: In a writing experiment with 453 professionals, not engineers, a model cut time by 40% and raised quality by 18%.
Sites above set energy use report measures to the energy authority every four years.

assumptions: Boundary: project reports and documentation; managing projects (task 18151) and graphical representations (task 18159) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s1: project status kept in the tracker through task 18151, for about 70% of projects; s1 is priced at that share.
Approving and sending keep their full time.
s2 keeps 70: the draft places measures, savings and status from the workbook, and the engineer writes the findings and checks the meaning of each statement.
research_questions: Are reports sent sooner without more client corrections?

incremental.description: Engineer keeps the report template current.
